referenceSources.description:
A striking red Fiat Cinquecento Trofeo, adorned with bold yellow and blue racing graphics and the number 97, sits on a gravel surface in front of a closed garage door. Sponsor logos including FIAT, TURIN, and MICHELIN appear on the rear bumper and side panels, while Abarth wheels and a visible roll cage hint at its rally-ready modifications.

Originally introduced in 1991 as a city car, the Cinquecento Trofeo emerged in 1992 as a single-make rally series contender. This 1996 Greek-converted example is one of just 14 Trofeo-spec models, featuring a 55 bhp engine upgrade, reinforced clutch, improved cooling, Bilstein suspension, Sparco steering wheel, bucket seats, and underbody paneling. Weighing only 790 kg, it was built for both track and rally competition, with championship winners earning a Monte-Carlo rally seat. The current owner has temporarily removed the front half of the roll cage for road use, which can be reinstalled for full rally compliance.
